definitions.def: to reach or get to something so you can use it
to get back information stored in your memory
knowing or noticing that something exists
the greatest amount that is allowed or possible
to form a picture of something in your mind

grammar_choice.en_template: The big difference between working and long-term memory is {{1:that/what}} we are explicitly aware of the information in working memory, but we are not {{2:able/possible}} to directly access the information in our long-term memory.
grammar_choice.ko_full: 작업 기억과 장기 기억의 큰 차이는, 우리가 작업 기억 속 정보는 명시적으로 인식하지만 장기 기억 속 정보에는 직접 접근할 수 없다는 것이다.
explain: is의 보어 명사절을 이끄는 접속사 that(완전한 절).
be able to + 동사원형 — 사람 주어 we는 able(possible 불가).

grammar_choice.en_template: We access long-term memory by {{1:bringing/bring}} the information into working memory.
grammar_choice.ko_full: 우리는 정보를 작업 기억으로 불러옴으로써 장기 기억에 접근한다.

grammar_choice.en_template: For example, right now you are not {{1:aware/awareness}} of all the actors you {{2:have/has}} ever seen.
grammar_choice.ko_full: 예를 들어, 지금 당신은 당신이 본 적 있는 모든 배우를 인식하고 있지는 않다.
explain: be 동사 보어 자리 — 형용사 aware(명사 awareness 불가).
주어 you + 현재완료 → have ever seen.

grammar_choice.en_template: They {{1:are stored/store}} in your long-term memory {{2:outside/outsider}} your consciousness.
grammar_choice.ko_full: 그들은 당신의 의식 밖, 당신의 장기 기억 속에 저장되어 있다.
explain: 주어 They는 '저장되는' 대상 → 수동태 are stored.

grammar_choice.en_template: However, if I {{1:asked/ask}} you to list all the actors, you {{2:would/will}} use your working memory to retrieve them one by one and reel them off.
grammar_choice.ko_full: 그러나 만약 내가 당신에게 모든 배우를 나열해 보라고 한다면, 당신은 작업 기억을 사용해 그들을 하나씩 떠올려 줄줄이 말할 것이다.
explain: 가정법 과거: If S + 과거동사 asked.

grammar_choice.en_template: Your working memory can {{1:access/accesses}} your long-term memory and {{2:bring/brings}} those memories to awareness.
grammar_choice.ko_full: 당신의 작업 기억은 장기 기억에 접근해 그 기억들을 의식으로 가져올 수 있다.
explain: can access ~ and (can) bring ~ 병렬 → 동사원형 bring.

grammar_choice.en_template: But {{1:remember/remembering}} it {{2:has/have}} a limit of seven items or chunks.
grammar_choice.ko_full: 그러나 그것이 일곱 개의 항목 또는 덩어리라는 한계를 가진다는 점을 기억하라.
각 배우는 하나의 항목이 될 것이다.

grammar_choice.en_template: Try and {{1:hold/holding}} all the actors you {{2:know/knows}} in your explicit awareness.
grammar_choice.ko_full: 당신이 아는 모든 배우를 명시적 인식 속에 붙잡아 두려고 해 보라.
explain: Try and + 동사원형(= try to) → hold.

grammar_choice.en_template: You might {{1:try/tries}} to visualize a large group {{2:of/for}} them.
grammar_choice.ko_full: 당신은 그들의 큰 무리를 시각화하려 할 수도 있다.

grammar_choice.en_template: But you still would {{1:only/lonely}} be aware of a few actors at {{2:any/some}} one time.
grammar_choice.ko_full: 그러나 당신은 여전히 한 번에 단지 몇 명의 배우만 인식할 수 있을 것이다.
explain: at any one time(한 번에) — 관용 표현.

jumble.answer: The big difference between working and long-term memory is that we are explicitly aware of the information in working memory, but we are not able to directly access the information in our long-term memory.
We access long-term memory by bringing the information into working memory.
For example, right now you are not aware of all the actors you have ever seen.
They are stored in your long-term memory outside your consciousness.
However, if I asked you to list all the actors, you would use your working memory to retrieve them one by one and reel them off.
Your working memory can access your long-term memory and bring those memories to awareness.
But remember it has a limit of seven items or chunks.
Each actor would be an item.
Try and hold all the actors you know in your explicit awareness.
You might try to visualize a large group of them.
But you still would only be aware of a few actors at any one time.
